observed_gap: Current RemoteEndpointEvidence deterministically hashes caller-supplied endpoint/capability/availability fields but has no explicit cryptographically verified peer-identity evidence, trust-root/issuer/credential generation or freshness/replay binding. Therefore current source validates field consistency and authority separation, not live peer authenticity.
expected_benefit: distinguish named endpoint evidence from authenticated peer evidence
fail closed on wrong/expired/stale peer credential instead of accepting syntactically valid endpoint fields
bind capability evidence to the authenticated peer and bridge protocol
make replay/freshness a testable invariant while preserving local canonical state/effect authority
retain optional local-first operation with substantially less runtime/dependency weight than full SPIRE
token_resource_implication: Expected negligible model-token impact; small deterministic schema/hash/test overhead. Full SPIRE is rejected at current scale because server+agent+registry+plugin lifecycle would add persistent CPU/RAM/ops/dependency surface without demonstrated F2 value.
counterhypothesis: An exact lower-layer bridge contract may already cryptographically authenticate/freshness-bind the endpoint and capability report. If found and source/receipt-bound, F2-WP-1106 should reference that contract rather than duplicate credential semantics.
falsifier_acceptance_gate: Locate an existing exact upstream contract that already binds live peer identity + credential freshness + capability evidence; if present, this delta collapses to a reference/integration test only.
Otherwise add the minimum native identity evidence contract and prove wrong peer, wrong root, stale/expired credential, capability mismatch and replayed session fail closed.
Prove DETACH/local boot remain independent of remote identity availability.
Prove successful peer authentication still grants zero canonical truth/effect/whole-system credit.
